q-73842.name: Question 1
q-73842.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=y\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+1$ at the point $(1,1,1).$
q-73842.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+1) \\  & =\frac{y}{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+1) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{x}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,1) & =\frac{1}{1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡1=1 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,1) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{1}{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-1 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,1)+(y-1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,1) \\ z-1 & =1\cdot (x-1)+1\cdot (y-1) \\ z-1 & =x+y-2 \\ -x-y+z+1 & =0 \\ x+y-z-1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-73842.html:
Question 1
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=yln⁡x+xln⁡y+1 at the point (1,1,1).

a
x+y−z−1=0
b
x−y−z+1=0
c
x−y+z−1=0
d
x+y−z−2=0
e
x+y+z−3=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as

z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0).

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(yln⁡x+xln⁡y+1)=yx+ln⁡y∂f∂y=∂∂y(yln⁡x+xln⁡y+1)=ln⁡x+xy

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at (x,y)=(1,1):

∂f∂x(1,1)=11+ln⁡1=1∂f∂y(1,1)=ln⁡1+11=1

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

z−1=(x−1)∂f∂x(1,1)+(y−1)∂f∂y(1,1)z−1=1⋅(x−1)+1⋅(y−1)z−1=x+y−2−x−y+z+1=0x+y−z−1=0

q-129445.name: Question 2
q-129445.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={x}^{3}{y}^{2}-2$ at the point $(1,2,2).$
q-129445.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}{y}^{2}-2) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{y}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}{y}^{2}-2) \\  & =2{x}^{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2) & =3({1}^{2})({2}^{2})=12 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) & =2({1}^{3})(2)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-2 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) \\ z-2 & =12(x-1)+4(y-2) \\ z-2 & =12x+4y-20 \\ 12x+4y-z-18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-129445.html:
Question 2
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=x3y2−2 at the point (1,2,2).

a
6x−4y+z=0
b
12x+4y−z−18=0
c
8x−y+z−8=0
d
12x−4y+z−6=0
e
6x+2y+z−12=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0).

First, we find the partial derivatives: ∂f∂x=∂∂x(x3y2−2)=3x2y2∂f∂y=∂∂y(x3y2−2)=2x3y

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at (x,y)=(1,2): ∂f∂x(1,2)=3(12)(22)=12∂f∂y(1,2)=2(13)(2)=4

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane: z−2=(x−1)∂f∂x(1,2)+(y−2)∂f∂y(1,2)z−2=12(x−1)+4(y−2)z−2=12x+4y−2012x+4y−z−18=0

q-129435.name: Question 3
q-129435.problem: Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=4{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}-7$ at the point $(1,-1,6).$
q-129435.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}-7) \\  & =8x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}-7) \\  & =18y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,-1) & =8(1)=8 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,-1) & =18(-1)=-18\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$

$$

Question 3
?

Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=4x2+9y2−7 at the point (1,−1,6).

a
4x−9y−z−7=0
b
4x+3y+z−7=0
c
2x+3y−z+7=0
d
8x−18y−z−20=0
e
8x+18y+z−16=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0).

First, we find the partial derivatives: ∂f∂x=∂∂x(4x2+9y2−7)=8x∂f∂y=∂∂y(4x2+9y2−7)=18y

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at (x,y)=(1,−1): ∂f∂x(1,−1)=8(1)=8∂f∂y(1,−1)=18(−1)=−18

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane: z−6=(x−1)∂f∂x(1,−1)+(y−(−1))∂f∂y(1,−1)z−6=8(x−1)−18(y+1)z−6=8x−18y−268x−18y−z−20=0

q-129439.name: Question 4
q-129439.problem: Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+3$ at the point $(0,1,1).$
q-129439.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+3) \\  & =2x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+3) \\  & =-4y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(0,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,1) & =2(0)=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,1) & =-4(1)=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-1 & =(x-0)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,1)+(y-1)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,1) \\ z-1 & =0x-4(y-1) \\ z-1 & =-4y+4 \\ 4y+z-5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-37721.name: Question 5
q-37721.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}-y$ at the point $(3,2,3).$
q-37721.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}-y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}}\cdot 2x-0 \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}-y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}}\cdot 2(3{y}^{2})-1 \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{3}}}-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(3,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(3,2) & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+2(2)^{3}}}=\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(3,2) & =\frac{3(2)^{2}}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+2(2)^{3}}}-1 \\  & =\frac{12}{5}-1 \\  & =\frac{7}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-3 & =(x-3)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(3,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(3,2) \\ z-3 & =\frac{3}{5}(x-3)+\frac{7}{5}(y-2) \\ 5z-15 & =3(x-3)+7(y-2) \\ 5z-15 & =3x-9+7y-14 \\ -3x-7y+5z+8 & =0 \\ 3x+7y-5z-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=x2+2y3−y at the point (3,2,3).

a
7x+3y−5z−8=0
b
7x−3y−8z−5=0
c
3x−7y+5z+8=0
d
5x+2y−5z+8=0
e
3x+7y−5z−8=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as

z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0).

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(x2+2y3−y)=12x2+2y3⋅2x−0=xx2+2y3∂f∂y=∂∂y(x2+2y3−y)=12x2+2y3⋅2(3y2)−1=3y2x2+2y3−1

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at (x,y)=(3,2):

∂f∂x(3,2)=332+2(2)3=35∂f∂y(3,2)=3(2)232+2(2)3−1=125−1=75

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

z−3=(x−3)∂f∂x(3,2)+(y−2)∂f∂y(3,2)z−3=35(x−3)+75(y−2)5z−15=3(x−3)+7(y−2)5z−15=3x−9+7y−14−3x−7y+5z+8=03x+7y−5z−8=0
